editorial.basis: The citation is an abstract with no formal description.  The Chinese text on page 4 gives a basic description but also indicates only an intention (拟建立, "plans to erect") regarding the new genus, and does not assign a type or other species.  The plate caption was intended to reassign Rotadiscus guizhouensis Zhao and Zhu 1994, but this is not formally stated and the species name was given incorrectly; no other source credits this publication for Pararotadiscus. Pararotadiscus is properly credited to Zhu, Zhao, & Chen (2002), which references this paper as if it stated Rotadiscus here.

notes: Latin name printed in the Chinese section on page 4 and the plate caption on page 13.  The English translation on page 11 mentions only Rotadiscus and not Pararotadiscus. Classified as "medusiform animals" in the English section, with the Chinese section using a word equivalent to Lophophorata and citing Dzik et al. 1997 which assigns the taxa in question to Lophophorata. The Chinese section also lists the appropriate included phyla for Lophophorata (Bryozoa, Brachiopoda, Phoronida, and Entoprocta).

notes: Apparently intended to reference Rotadiscus guizhouensis Zhao & Zhu 1994, which in 2002 was validly recombined as Pararotadiscus guizhouensis. The lack of a "n. sp." and the parentheses around (Zhao and Zhu, 1994) indicate a recombination instead of a new taxon, and there are two other "taijiangensis" species on the page that may be sources of the confusion.  Both "taijiangensis" and "guizhouensis" are also place-based names. Neither species is given in the Chinese text; only the genus is mentioned.  Therefore this is treated as a lapsus calami rather than a nomen nudum at the species level.
